units.text: RFC 9110 requires that a HEAD response must not include a message body, even though it includes headers describing what would have been sent.

judgement.reason: The passages state RFC 9110 requires a HEAD response to omit the message body, while headers such as Content-Length describe the body that would have been returned for GET.

units.text: The headers in a 200 HEAD response, such as Content-Length, reflect the body that would have been sent in a 200 GET response for the same resource.

judgement.reason: The second passage explicitly states that headers like Content-Length in a HEAD response describe the body that would have been returned for a GET, with the actual body omitted.

units.text: Because the GET response includes the actual body and the HEAD response omits it, the GET response carries more body bytes than the HEAD response.

judgement.reason: The passages state HEAD omits the response body while GET includes the body that HEAD would have returned, so GET carries more body bytes.
